blocks.x: Clinicians get 90 minutes a day back — ambient documentation inside the EHR
A 12-hospital US health system — Healthcare & Life Sciences engagement delivered by a 18-person team over 11 months, US scope, commercial model: build-transfer.

items: Physicians documented 3+ hours daily; burnout metrics deteriorating across specialties.
Prior AI tools stalled at EHR integration and compliance review.
PHI estate faced ransomware exposure from legacy devices and vendor access.

blocks.x: We deployed ambient documentation integrated into the EHR with clinician sign-off, grounded on specialty-specific note templates and governed by the clinical AI board on Compass (model cards, evaluations, oversight gates). A parallel security program segmented medical devices and rehearsed clinical-continuity recovery — including a manual-fallback drill per department.

What the delivery actually looks like week to week: weeks 1–2 produce the signed baseline: current per 1,000 patients performance, method note, and a control owner who co-signs every later claim. from week 3 the working slice goes live at product line scope: shadow first, then canary, then promoted cohorts — each promotion justified by the eval gate, not enthusiasm. The design principle here is simple: the decision path and the audit path share one timeline across Healthcare & Life Sciences, so your control owners can interrogate any number we publish.. At operating tempo, the properties that carry the load are structural: every state change is replayable from the signed baseline in Data, Analytics & Lakehouse delivery, which keeps the blast radius of any change inside one lane.

items: The delta we sign up to is down 28 — verified against live data at every gate
Target range up 26 on the first working slice, with the method note attached
